notes.title: 001 — Mission, guardrails, and success criteria
notes.thesis: The ideal solution to global warming is not one heroic technology but a disciplined global portfolio that cuts gross emissions fast, protects sinks, limits overshoot, and stays politically durable.

notes.title: 002 — The fast stack: clean power, electrification, and efficiency
notes.thesis: The fastest broad solution stack is abundant clean electricity plus electrification plus efficiency, because it cuts across power, transport, buildings, and part of industry at once.

notes.title: 003 — Hard sectors: industry, freight, shipping, and aviation
notes.thesis: The ideal solution is to electrify what is easy and reserve scarce expensive tools for hard sectors that truly need them.

notes.title: 004 — Methane, land, food, and forest systems
notes.thesis: A workable climate solution must treat methane and land systems as front-line levers, not leftovers after energy policy.

notes.title: 005 — Policy, finance, state capacity, and just transition
notes.thesis: Climate success is a coordination and investment problem as much as a technology problem, so the ideal solution must build durable political coalitions and public capacity.

notes.title: 006 — Carbon removal, overshoot, and the research frontier
notes.thesis: Carbon dioxide removal belongs in the solution only as a bounded residual tool; the more the world delays gross cuts, the riskier and larger the required removal portfolio becomes.

notes.title: 007 — Delivery architecture: abundance, retirement, and development
notes.thesis: The ideal solution is not just a technology portfolio but a delivery bargain: wealthy countries move first on fossil retirement and finance, while emerging and low-income economies get rapid clean-development buildout, energy access, and institutional support.

notes.title: 008 — Managed fossil decline: retirement, sequencing, and subsidy reform
notes.thesis: Solving global warming requires not only building clean systems fast but also explicitly managing the decline of coal, oil, and gas so clean additions displace fossil use rather than merely accompany it.

notes.title: 009 — Outcome metrics: absolute cuts, displacement, and access
notes.thesis: The archive should judge climate solutions by a short scoreboard of physical outcomes and access conditions, not by pledge counts, dollars announced, or intensity improvements alone.

notes.title: 010 — Throughput constraints: grids, permitting, supply chains, and local legitimacy
notes.thesis: The world’s climate problem is now constrained as much by throughput as by technology: it has to permit, procure, connect, and legitimate clean infrastructure faster than fossil incumbency and administrative drag can stall it.

notes.title: 011 — Climate observability: MRV, open data, and public proof
notes.thesis: The ideal climate solution needs public observability as well as good policy: emissions, deforestation, methane leaks, and delivery claims have to be measured quickly enough and openly enough to drive correction before another year is lost.

notes.title: 012 — Time discipline: first-decade sequencing, lock-in, and earned residuals
notes.thesis: The ideal climate solution is not only a portfolio but a sequence: the first decade must be dominated by the fastest, highest-confidence emissions cuts and by decisions that avoid new fossil and infrastructure lock-in, while slower hard-sector transformations and residual cleanup are developed without being allowed to delay near-term action.

notes.title: 013 — Reliability architecture: flexibility, storage, demand response, and clean firming
notes.thesis: A decarbonized power system has to be designed for reliability and affordability on purpose — through flexibility, storage, demand response, technical stability, and some dispatchable clean or tightly governed transitional capacity — or else rapid clean buildout can harden into curtailment, price volatility, backlash, and fossil relapse.

notes.title: 014 — Adoption architecture: defaults, zero-upfront finance, installers, and low-friction switching
notes.thesis: An ideal climate solution has to make clean switching the low-friction default for households and small firms — through zero- or low-upfront finance, simple replacement pathways, installer capacity, renter-safe rules, product standards, and public charging and service access — rather than assuming people will navigate high capital costs, paperwork, and contractor scarcity on their own.

notes.title: 015 — Lead markets, standards, procurement, and coordinated trade rules
notes.thesis: An ideal climate solution has to create **lead markets for clean materials and fuels** — with public procurement, advance offtake, interoperable product standards, credible carbon accounting, and coordinated trade rules — so first movers in steel, cement, chemicals, and other hard sectors are rewarded for decarbonising rather than undercut by cheaper high-emissions production.

notes.title: 016 — Innovation discipline: demonstrations, first-of-a-kind projects, and no-delay learning
notes.thesis: An ideal climate solution must pair **deployment of mature tools at full speed** with a disciplined public pipeline for demonstrations and first-of-a-kind projects in the technologies that are still not ready at commercial scale — without letting frontier innovation become an excuse to delay fast cuts.

notes.title: 017 — Spatial systems: compact cities, transit, retrofit-first growth, and structural demand reduction
notes.thesis: An ideal climate solution must shape **where people live, how they move, and what gets built** — through compact urban growth, public and active transport, retrofit-first building policy, and whole-life carbon rules — because electrification alone cannot outrun sprawl, floor-area expansion, and car dependence.

notes.title: 018 — Material throughput: circularity, reuse, repair, and long-life design
notes.thesis: An ideal climate solution must cut **virgin material demand** through circular design, reuse, repair, retrofit, longer product lifetimes, and better material productivity, because clean supply alone cannot decarbonize an economy that keeps demanding ever more steel, cement, plastics, and waste.

notes.title: 019 — Non-CO₂ completion: nitrous oxide, refrigerants, and sustainable cooling
notes.thesis: An ideal climate solution must **complete the non-CO₂ strategy** by attacking nitrous oxide and high-GWP refrigerants while expanding sustainable cooling access, because methane alone does not close the fast-warming gap.

notes.title: 020 — Workforce architecture: skills, apprenticeships, reskilling, and service capacity
notes.thesis: An ideal climate solution needs an explicit **workforce architecture** — training pipelines, apprenticeships, reskilling, recruitment, retention, job quality, and inclusion — because grids, retrofits, heat pumps, EVs, cooling systems, and clean industry are built, operated, and maintained by skilled people, not by capital and hardware alone.
